transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, it's my job. I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work down at the dry cleaners, and... well, we get so busy, especially when the seasons change. Just the other day, Mrs. Gable brought in this heavy wool coat that smelled exactly like wet dog, and I was trying to tell her that we need to treat the lining differently, but she just wouldn't listen. People never listen about the linings, they just expect miracles. 

But anyway, what I mean is... my station is just a complete disaster lately. I have all the claim tickets, the cash receipts, my workshop notes, and the actual customer jobs just piled all together in this massive heap. I stand there looking at it all, and I honestly do not know what to handle first. It's just a mountain of stuff. And don't even get me started on when the delivery driver comes in and drops off the wire hangers, because they always put the boxes right in the middle of my sorting area, and I keep telling them to leave it by the back door... but yeah, I just can't keep things straight.
Do you find yourself thinking about work or the organization of your station when you're not at the dry cleaners?

I haven't really noticed if I do. Honestly, when I leave there, my brain is just kind of... fried, so I don't really keep track of what's in my head. I usually take the bus home, the number 14, and there's always this one guy on there who plays his music out loud. Just right out of his phone speaker! I don't understand why people do that, they make headphones for a reason, you know? 

My niece got me these nice wireless ones for my birthday last year, the little white ones that go right in your ear. I was so worried I was going to lose them down a drain or something because they're just so small. But they really do block out the noise. I wore them to the grocery store once and didn't even hear the cashier asking for my loyalty card. I felt terrible, she was just standing there waiting on me. But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, thinking about work at home. Yeah, I don't know, I guess I just haven't really paid attention to whether I do or not.
Do you often find yourself getting sidetracked by things around you, like the man playing music on the bus?

Well, I mean... I don't know if I'd say "sidetracked," but I definitely notice things. Like the music, yes, but also just... everything. Like the other day, I was walking to the bus stop, and I saw this stray cat by the dumpster behind the bakery. It was an orange tabby, just a little thing, and it looked so hungry. I almost went into the bakery to buy it a croissant or something, but then I remembered cats probably shouldn't eat butter, right? Or maybe they can, I don't know. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she has three cats, and she feeds them this special diet food that smells awful, like old fish. She leaves the cans out on her porch sometimes, and the raccoons get into them. Raccoons are so clever with their little hands, aren't they? They figured out how to open my trash can even when I put a brick on top of it. I had to buy one of those bungee cords to keep it shut. But um... yeah, I don't really know if I get sidetracked more than anyone else. I just... I notice what's going on around me, I guess.
Do you have trouble finishing tasks once you start them?

Well, yeah, I suppose I do. Like, if my manager gives me three things to do—say, call the supplier about the hangers, tag that silk blouse that came in yesterday, and enter the receipts into the register—I'll usually get the first one done. I'll call the supplier, and then... well, while I'm on the phone, I'll notice a stain on the counter, and I'll start scrubbing it. We use this citrus cleaner, it smells just like real oranges, not that fake chemical smell, you know? It reminds me of the orange trees my grandmother had in her backyard in Florida. She used to make fresh juice every morning, and she had this old glass juicer that you had to press down on really hard. I always wanted to help, but my hands were too small. 

Anyway, I'll be scrubbing the counter, and then a customer will walk in, and by the time I'm done helping them, I completely forget about the silk blouse and the receipts. I just get pulled into whatever is right in front of me, and the other things just... slip away. My manager gets so frustrated, she leaves these sticky notes everywhere, but even those end up under a pile of tickets. Sticky notes are terrible anyway, the glue never holds up if it's humid, and it gets so muggy in the shop with the steam presses running. I bought a little desk fan, but it just blows the tickets around... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, finishing tasks. Yeah, I guess I do have trouble getting to the end of a list.
Do you have any habits or things you do over and over that you feel like you can't stop doing?

Habits I can't stop? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I have anything like that. I do tap my foot a lot when I'm sitting down, but that's just because I have a lot of energy, I guess. My sister used to hate it when we shared a room growing up. She'd always yell at me to stop shaking the floor. We had this old wooden floor in our bedroom, real hardwood, not that laminate stuff they put in houses now. It was beautiful, but it creaked so loudly if you stepped in the wrong spot. You had to memorize where the squeaky boards were if you wanted to sneak down to the kitchen for a midnight snack. My dad was a light sleeper, and if he caught us, he'd make us do chores the next day. One time I had to weed the entire garden just because I wanted a glass of milk. But anyway, no, I don't really have any habits I feel like I *have* to do, you know? Just regular fidgeting, I guess.
Do you ever have thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind?

Repeating thoughts? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, my mind is definitely noisy, but it's not like a broken record playing the exact same thing over and over. It's more like... it just jumps around. 

Like, the other day I was pressing a pair of slacks at work—these really nice heavy wool ones, and you have to be so careful with the steam on wool or it starts to smell exactly like a wet dog. My neighbor's dog got out in the rain last week, actually. A little terrier mix, I think. Anyway, he was covered in mud and shook it all over her front porch. She had just painted that porch, too! A really pretty robin's egg blue. I always wanted a blue porch, but my ex-husband, he said it looked tacky. He only liked neutral colors, so everything in our house was beige or gray. It was so dull. I bought a bright red throw pillow once on sale at Target, and he threw an absolute fit about it clashing with the rug. He was so picky about the strangest things, always complaining about the way I folded his socks... 

But um, wait, what were you asking me? Oh, thoughts repeating. Yeah, no, I don't really get stuck on one thought. It's always just a bunch of different ones moving past.
Do you often feel nervous or anxious about things that are happening in your life?

Nervous or anxious? I mean, I guess I have normal worries, but I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person. I don't sit around chewing my nails about the future or anything. I just take things as they come. 

Like yesterday, the big commercial washing machine broke down right in the middle of a load of hotel sheets. The belt just snapped—made this awful slapping sound. But I didn't panic. I just called the repair guy. His name is Frank, he's been fixing our machines for years. He always wears these suspenders, the heavy-duty kind with the metal clips. My grandfather used to wear suspenders just like that. He was a carpenter, and he had this huge tool belt that he’d wear over them. I loved the smell of his workshop, all that fresh sawdust and wood glue. He made me a little wooden rocking horse for my fifth birthday. It had a real yarn mane that my grandmother braided. She was always knitting or crocheting something. She made these beautiful afghans, the kind with the zigzag pattern, you know? Chevron, I think it's called. She made a yellow and brown one that we kept on the back of the sofa for years. It was so scratchy, though, because she used that cheap acrylic yarn that you could buy in bulk at the craft store... 

Sorry, what was the question? Oh, being nervous. No, I don't really get nervous about things. I just kind of deal with whatever happens.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by your surroundings when you're trying to focus on a task?

Distracted by my surroundings? Um, no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, I usually just get my work done. 

Like when I'm sorting the incoming dry cleaning, you have to really focus on checking all the pockets before anything goes in the machine. People leave the craziest things in their pockets. Just Tuesday, I found a whole handful of peppermint candies in this guy's suit jacket. You know, the ones with the red and white swirls wrapped in that crinkly plastic? My aunt Linda always kept those exact same mints in her purse. Her purse was this massive brown leather tote bag, weighed an absolute ton. She said it was real Italian leather, but I'm pretty sure she bought it at the flea market out on Route 9. We used to go to that flea market every Sunday morning when I was a teenager. You could get the absolute best funnel cake there. They'd fry it right in front of you and just bury it in powdered sugar. I tried making funnel cake at home once for my kids, but the oil got way too hot and set off the smoke detector. The fire department actually showed up because it was wired to the alarm company. The fire captain was this really tall guy, very handsome, looked a little like Tom Selleck. He had that exact same thick mustache... 

Um, wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being distracted. No, I don't really have a problem with that. I just do what I need to do.
Do you find it hard to keep your attention on one task for a long time?

Hard to keep my attention on one thing? Yeah, I guess that happens a lot. Like, I can start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine, you know, checking the tickets against the garments. But after a few minutes, my mind is just... off. I'll start looking at the clothing labels, wondering where they bought it. There was this one silk blouse yesterday with a label from a boutique in Paris, France. Can you imagine going to Paris just to buy a shirt? I've always wanted to go to Europe. My cousin went to Italy for her honeymoon and brought back all these pictures of old churches. The architecture over there is just incredible. It made me think about our church choir, actually. I'm supposed to be picking out the hymns for next Sunday's service, and I keep going back and forth between "Amazing Grace" and "How Great Thou Art." "Amazing Grace" is a classic, but the altos always struggle with that one high note in the third verse. We had a substitute organist last week who played everything in the wrong key, and it was just a disaster. The whole congregation sounded like a flock of geese... 

Oh, what was I saying? Right, the dry-cleaning orders. Yeah, so I'll be thinking about the choir plans or something I need to fix at home, and then I realize I've been standing there for ten minutes and missed half of the tickets I was supposed to check. It's just hard to stay on that one thing for very long.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?

Act on impulse? No, I wouldn't say I do that. I mean, I don't just go out and buy a new car on a whim or anything crazy like that. I'm pretty sensible. 

Like with grocery shopping, I always make a list. You have to make a list, especially with the prices these days. Eggs are just outrageous right now. I remember when you could get a dozen eggs for under a dollar. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she actually started keeping chickens in her backyard because she was so fed up with the grocery store prices. She’s got three of them—Rhode Island Reds, I think she said. They're actually quite pretty birds, all glossy and brown. But they cluck so loudly in the morning. It wakes up my cat, Barnaby. Barnaby is a Maine Coon mix, huge orange tabby. He used to be a stray, just showed up on my porch one winter looking half-starved. I started leaving out little bowls of tuna for him. You really shouldn't give cats too much tuna, though, because of the mercury. I read an article about that in one of those magazines at the dentist's office. My dentist, Dr. Evans, has the most beautiful waiting room. He has this massive saltwater aquarium right in the middle of it. It's got these little yellow tangs and clownfish. It's so relaxing to watch them just swimming around the coral. I always thought about getting an aquarium, but the maintenance just seems like so much work, cleaning the filters and checking the pH levels...

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Acting on impulse? No, I don't really do that. I'm pretty careful about things.
Do you find that you can focus on a task for a short while, but then your attention starts to wander?

Focus for a short while? Yeah, I think I just mentioned that, actually. Like with the dry-cleaning orders. I can start off perfectly fine, you know, checking the tickets against the clothes, making sure the names match up. But then, it's just like a switch flips after a few minutes. I'll be looking at a label, and my mind is just... off. 

Like, I'll start thinking about the choir plans for church, or maybe remembering that I need to fix the hinge on the kitchen cabinet at home. My husband was supposed to fix that hinge three weeks ago, but he's been so busy with his fantasy football league. I don't understand fantasy football at all. You're just picking players from different teams and pretending they play together? It makes no sense. He gets so worked up about it, too. Last Sunday, he was yelling at the TV because some guy from the Green Bay Packers dropped a pass. I've never even been to Wisconsin, but I heard they have amazing cheese curds. You can get them fried, kind of like the funnel cakes at the flea market... 

Oh, right, sorry. The orders. Yeah, so I'll be thinking about the choir or the cabinet, and then I realize I've just been standing there holding a pair of slacks for ten minutes, and I've completely lost my place and missed half the tickets I was supposed to check. It just wanders off, my attention.
Do you find it easier to focus on tasks when they are broken down into smaller, more manageable steps?

Smaller steps? Hmm, I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if that helps or not. I suppose it might? But I usually just try to tackle things as they come. 

Like when I'm doing the pressing at work. You just grab the next shirt on the rack. The shirts are mostly cotton blends these days, not like the heavy starched collars they used to wear. My grandfather used to wear those stiff collars every single day to his job at the bank. He was a teller for forty years. Can you imagine doing the exact same thing for forty years? He got a gold watch when he retired. It was a pocket watch, actually, with his initials engraved on the back. My brother Tommy has it now. Tommy collects watches, he’s got a whole display case full of them in his den. He even has one of those old Mickey Mouse watches with the arms that move to tell the time. I always thought those were so cute. I used to watch the Mickey Mouse Club when I was a little girl. Annette Funicello was my favorite. She had that beautiful dark hair. I tried to curl my hair like hers once for a school dance, but I used too much of that setting lotion and my hair was crunchy for three days. I smelled like a walking beauty parlor... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, breaking things down into steps. Yeah, I don't really know if I do that. I just sort of do the work as it's there.
Do you find it hard to stick with one activity for a long period of time without feeling restless or bored?

Restless or bored? Hmm. No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really get bored, to be honest. There's always something to keep busy with, you know? 

Like at the cleaners, if I'm not pressing shirts, I'm untangling the hangers. We get mountains of those wire hangers returned to us. People just bring them in by the armful. Joan, she's the manager there, she absolutely hates the wire ones because they get hooked on everything. She prefers the thick plastic ones. I actually bought a whole set of those velvet-covered hangers for my own closet at home. They're supposed to keep your blouses from slipping off the ends. I got them on QVC. I just love watching QVC late at night. The hosts are so chatty, it's like having company right there in the living room. Last week they were selling this copper frying pan, said nothing would ever stick to it, not even burnt cheese. I almost bought it, but I already have a perfectly good cast iron skillet. My grandmother gave me that skillet when I first moved out. She used to make the best cornbread in it. Real Southern style, you know, absolutely no sugar. People put sugar in cornbread nowadays and it just tastes like a cupcake. If I want a cupcake, I'll go down to the bakery. There's a new one that just opened up next to the pharmacy, and they make these little lemon tarts that are just... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Feeling restless? No, I don't think I really get restless or bored like that.
Do you often find that you can focus at the beginning of a task, but then struggle to maintain that focus as time goes on?

Focus at the beginning, but then struggle later? Yeah, I think we were just talking about that, weren't we? It's exactly like with the dry-cleaning orders. I can start off perfectly fine, going through the tickets for the day, making sure everything is in order. But then, it's just like my brain decides to take a walk. 

After a few minutes, I'll be looking at a tag on a blouse, and suddenly I'm not thinking about the order at all. I'm looking at the brand label, wondering where it was made, or I'm thinking about the choir practice we have on Thursday night. We're doing a new arrangement of "Amazing Grace" and the sopranos are really struggling with the high notes in the third verse. Brenda, she's our lead soprano, she insists she can hit it, but last week it sounded like a cat caught in a screen door. I felt so bad for her, but I had to bite the inside of my cheek to keep from laughing. You know how it is when you're in church and you're not supposed to laugh? It just makes it ten times funnier. My cousin Jimmy used to make funny faces at me during the sermon when we were kids, and I'd end up snorting out loud. My mother would pinch my arm so hard it would leave a little red mark for two days. She always wore these beautiful pearl earrings to church, real cultured pearls my dad got her for their tenth anniversary...

Oh, goodness, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm sorry. What were we saying? Right, the orders. So, yeah, I'll start thinking about the choir or something I need to do at home, and then I'll snap back and realize I've just been staring at the same pile of clothes, and I've completely missed half the tickets I was supposed to be checking. It just slips right away from me.
Do you find that you are able to focus on a task for a short period, but then your attention starts to fade as time goes on?

I feel like we might have just covered this one, Doctor! But yes, it's exactly what I was just saying. It's like my attention just evaporates. I can start off checking the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine, but it only lasts a short little bit. Then my mind is totally gone—off on the choir plans or whatever chores I have waiting for me at home. 

Like, I just remembered I need to take the chicken out of the freezer for dinner. I usually buy the big family pack of thighs when they go on sale at the Piggly Wiggly. They had a huge sale on Tuesday, buy one get one free. I actually ran into Shirley in the meat aisle, she sings alto in our choir. She was telling me all about her daughter's wedding. They're doing one of those rustic barn weddings, which are so popular right now, with the mason jars and the string lights everywhere. I think it sounds like a terrible fire hazard, honestly, all that old dry wood and hot electricity. My uncle had a barn catch fire once when I was a teenager, lost a brand new John Deere tractor. The smoke was so thick you could see it from three towns over... 

Oh, heavens, I'm rambling again, aren't I? I'm so sorry. But yes, that's exactly how it happens at work. My attention fades out, I start thinking about Shirley or the grocery store, and the next thing I know, I've missed half the tickets I was supposed to be checking.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when things don't go as planned?

Controlling my emotions? Hmm, no, I wouldn't say that. I'm usually pretty even-keeled, even if things get a little mixed up. Like, if the delivery truck is late at the cleaners, I don't throw a fit or anything. Carl, our driver, he is always running behind on Tuesdays. He blames the construction on Route 9, but I know for a fact he stops at that little diner over by the interstate. You can't blame him, really, they have this cherry pie that is just out of this world. The crust is so flaky, it just melts. My husband used to eat half a pie by himself when we first got married, but he can't have all that sugar now, and his teeth give him trouble with the crust anyway. He finally went to Dr. Henderson about that back molar last week. Dr. Henderson is a saint, honestly, he's been our dentist for twenty years. He always has those old magazines in the waiting room, though. I was reading one from 2018 about how to organize your pantry with matching glass jars. I tried that once, put all my flour and sugar in these beautiful big jars I found at a yard sale, but they were so heavy I could barely lift them off the top shelf without feeling like I was going to drop them on my toes... 

Anyway, I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. Were you asking if I get mad? No, I don't really get too upset when plans change. I just kind of roll with it.
Do you find it harder to pay attention to a task the longer you've been doing it?

I feel like I'm a broken record today, Doctor! But yes, it really does get harder the longer I sit there. Like I was saying before, I can start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine. The first few tickets, I'm right there, checking the dates, checking the starch requests. But after a few minutes, my mind is just gone. 

I'll be looking at the clothes, but I'm actually thinking about the labels, or those choir plans I mentioned, or if I left the porch light on at home. We had a string of break-ins in the neighborhood over the summer, mostly just kids looking for unlocked cars, but it makes you nervous. My neighbor, Mr. Abernathy, he installed these massive floodlights on his garage that are so bright they shine right into my guest bedroom window. I had to go out and buy blackout curtains just so my sister could sleep when she came to visit for Thanksgiving. She always comes for Thanksgiving because her husband refuses to fly, and the drive from Ohio is just too much for him with his sciatica. He tried one of those special cushions you see on TV, the ones with the honeycomb gel inside, but he said it just made him feel like he was sitting on a waffle iron... 

Oh, for crying out loud, I've wandered off again. I'm sorry. But yes, the longer I try to look at those orders, the harder it gets. I'll snap out of my daydream about my brother-in-law's sciatica or whatever, and realize I've completely missed half of what I was supposed to check. It's like my brain just can't hold on to it for more than a couple of minutes.
Do you find that you are more easily distracted or have trouble focusing when you've been working on a task for a longer period of time?

Oh, my goodness, Doctor, I think you might be asking me the same thing again! But yes, absolutely. It's exactly like I was just saying. If I'm working on something for a while, my focus just packs up and leaves. 

I'll sit down with the dry-cleaning orders, and I'm totally fine at first. But a few minutes go by, and suddenly I'm not looking at the tickets anymore. I'm staring at the care labels and wondering who invented the little symbols, or I'm planning out the hymns for Sunday service, or I'm worrying about whether I left a window open at the house. We had that awful thunderstorm last week, the one that knocked down the big oak tree over by the library. The poor librarian, Mrs. Higgins, she had just parked her Buick under it not ten minutes before. Completely crushed the roof. It was a beautiful car, too, a 1998 LeSabre, she kept it in immaculate condition. She always used to bring us her husband's wool suits to clean, even though he passed away five years ago. She just likes having them fresh in the closet, I suppose. Grief does funny things to people. When my mother passed, I couldn't stop baking. I must have made fifty loaves of banana bread that first month. I was giving it to the mailman, the paperboy, anyone who walked past the house...

Oh, dear me. I've done it again, haven't I? I am so sorry. But yes, to answer your question, the longer I sit there with those orders, the more distracted I get. I'll snap out of thinking about Mrs. Higgins' Buick or whatever, and I'll realize I've completely missed half the tickets I was supposed to be checking. It just gets so much harder to pay attention the longer I do it.
Do you think your difficulty in focusing and completing tasks is causing significant problems in your daily life or relationships?

Well, yes, I suppose it is causing some real headaches. At the shop, it's gotten pretty bad. We've had late orders because I lose track of time, and the billing... oh, the billing gets so confused when I'm trying to sort it out. I've had some really tense moments with the staff and even a few customers. It reminds me of this one lady, Mrs. Gable, she came in last Thursday looking for her husband's tuxedo. He had this big gala for the Rotary Club. They always do it at that fancy hotel downtown, the one with the big crystal chandeliers in the lobby. I went to a wedding there once, back in the eighties. The bride wore this dress with the biggest puffed sleeves you've ever seen, it looked like she had two white pumpkins on her shoulders. Her mother insisted on a chocolate fountain, which was a terrible idea because halfway through the reception, the groom's uncle—who had a bit too much champagne, mind you—bumped the table and chocolate went everywhere. It took them hours to clean the carpet, and I don't think they ever got the stain out of the bride's train...

Oh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yes, it's causing problems. Even at church, I've had to step back from leading some of the planning committees. People were just getting too frustrated with me forgetting things and getting off track. It's embarrassing, honestly.
Do you feel like your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks are affecting your overall quality of life?

Well, I guess that's really what it boils down to, isn't it? My quality of life. It's just... it's taking a toll. Like I mentioned, the shop is really suffering. I'm causing late orders, the billing is a complete mess half the time because I can't keep my head in it, and it's led to some really tense moments with the staff and the customers. 

And it's not just work, it's my church life, too. I've had to step back from leading the planning committees. People were getting so frustrated with me. Which breaks my heart, because I've been on the spring bazaar committee for fifteen years. We always do a bake sale, and my pecan pie is usually the first thing to go. I use my grandmother's recipe, the secret is a little splash of bourbon in the filling. Not enough to get anyone tipsy, just enough to cut the sweetness of the corn syrup. My grandmother used to hide her bourbon in an empty vanilla extract bottle in the pantry so my grandfather wouldn't drink it. He was a good man, but he loved his evening toddy a bit too much, especially after he retired from the railroad. He worked on the B&O line for forty years, started as a brakeman and worked his way up. They gave him a beautiful gold pocket watch when he retired, but he lost it fishing down at Miller's Pond about two weeks later... 

Oh, goodness gracious, I'm so sorry, Doctor. I've completely lost the thread again. But yes, to answer your question, it is affecting my life. It's just exhausting feeling like I'm letting everyone down, at the shop and at church, just because I can't keep my mind on what I'm doing.

But anyway, what I mean is... my station is just a complete disaster lately. I've had some really tense moments with the staff and even a few customers. It reminds me of this one lady, Mrs. Gable, she came in last Thursday looking for her husband's tuxedo. He had this big gala for the Rotary Club. They always do it at that fancy hotel downtown, the one with the big crystal chandeliers in the lobby. I went to a wedding there once, back in the eighties. The bride wore this dress with the biggest puffed sleeves you've ever seen, it looked like she had two white pumpkins on her shoulders. Her mother insisted on a chocolate fountain, which was a terrible idea because halfway through the reception, the groom's uncle—who had a bit too much champagne, mind you—bumped the table and chocolate went everywhere. It took them hours to clean the carpet, and I don't think they ever got the stain out of the bride's train...

Oh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yes, it's causing problems. Even at church, I've had to step back from leading some of the planning committees. People were just getting too frustrated with me forgetting things and getting off track. It's embarrassing, honestly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are significantly impacting their daily life
doctor.question: Do you feel like your difficulties with focusing and completing tasks are affecting your overall quality of life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: The shop has had late orders, confused billing, and tense moments with staff and customers, and at church I have stepped back from leading some planning because people were getting frustrated with me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how the symptoms are affecting the patient's overall quality of life, which directly addresses functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Well, I guess that's really what it boils down to, isn't it? My quality of life. It's just... it's taking a toll. Like I mentioned, the shop is really suffering. I'm causing late orders, the billing is a complete mess half the time because I can't keep my head in it, and it's led to some really tense moments with the staff and the customers. 

And it's not just work, it's my church life, too. I've had to step back from leading the planning committees. People were getting so frustrated with me. Which breaks my heart, because I've been on the spring bazaar committee for fifteen years. We always do a bake sale, and my pecan pie is usually the first thing to go. I use my grandmother's recipe, the secret is a little splash of bourbon in the filling. Not enough to get anyone tipsy, just enough to cut the sweetness of the corn syrup. My grandmother used to hide her bourbon in an empty vanilla extract bottle in the pantry so my grandfather wouldn't drink it. He was a good man, but he loved his evening toddy a bit too much, especially after he retired from the railroad. He worked on the B&O line for forty years, started as a brakeman and worked his way up. They gave him a beautiful gold pocket watch when he retired, but he lost it fishing down at Miller's Pond about two weeks later... 

Oh, goodness gracious, I'm so sorry, Doctor. I've completely lost the thread again. But yes, to answer your question, it is affecting my life. It's just exhausting feeling like I'm letting everyone down, at the shop and at church, just because I can't keep my mind on what I'm doing.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, disorganization, and difficulty sustaining focus on tasks are consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Type.
